one_liner: Multithreaded Rust lossless PNG/APNG optimizer; 2.2x (default) to 5x (-o4) faster than OptiPNG 0.7.7 wall-clock on one test image.
what_it_does: Oxipng rewrites existing PNG and APNG files losslessly to make them smaller: it tries bit-depth, color-type, palette and grayscale reductions, re-filters scanlines, recompresses IDAT, iCCP and other compressed chunks, optionally strips metadata, and keeps the result only if it is smaller. It is a CLI (oxipng -o 0..6|max, --strip, --alpha, --zopfli, -t threads, --dry-run) and a Rust crate with optimize(InFile, OutFile, &Options), optimize_from_memory(&[u8], &Options) and RawImage::create_optimized_png() for turning raw pixels into an optimized PNG. Its options resemble OptiPNG's, but the README says it is not a drop-in replacement.
how_it_is_fast: Three things, not one faster algorithm: (1) trials run in parallel on rayon, each reduction candidate and filter strategy in its own task, with a shared atomic best size (AtomicMin) passed to the deflater as an output cap so losing trials abort early; (2) compression uses libdeflate (levels 10-12 are its near-optimal parser) instead of zlib; (3) in the default fast-evaluation mode (levels 0-4) reductions and filter strategies are ranked with a cheap libdeflate level (5, 7 or 8 per optimize_raw) and only the winner is compressed once at the main level (11 at -o2, 12 at -o4). Filter strategies include the five PNG filters plus heuristic MinSum, Entropy, Bigrams, BigEnt and a Brute strategy that test-compresses a few lines per row choice.
when_to_use: Build, CI or pre-commit steps that losslessly shrink PNG assets; the project ships a pre-commit hook and a ghcr.io Docker image for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.

Interactive or few-file runs on a multi-core machine where wall-clock time matters: one image's trials spread across cores, giving 2.22x at the default level and 5.01x at -o4 against single-threaded OptiPNG on a 20-thread i7-12700 in the README run.

Replacing OptiPNG in image pipelines where the default level should also compress better: the op111.net comparison (search snippet only) reports 29.14% versus 25.42% size reduction on d3js.org.png at about 3.5x the speed.
Rust programs that produce or post-process PNGs in memory: optimize_from_memory() or RawImage plus Options::from_preset(level), with --max-raw-size and timeout controls available.
Web or WASM image tools: Squoosh and jSquash use it per the README, and a freestanding feature forwards to libdeflater for targets without a full libc.
when_not_to_use: Batch jobs that already run one OptiPNG process per core: then the parallel trials add little and the gain falls toward the CPU-time ratio, which was only 1.71x (default) and 1.65x (-o4) in the README run (derived from page data).

Maximum compression at any cost: oxipng is not a brute-force optimizer, so a higher level can occasionally give a larger file and --zopfli is not guaranteed to help; op111 (snippet only) shows --opt max --zopfli taking 28.9 s for 30.25% versus 0.764 s for 29.14% at the default on the same image. ECT or other zopfli-based tools trade more time for bytes.

Animated PNGs: APNG support is limited to alpha optimization, refiltering and recompression with all reductions disabled; the README recommends running apngopt first, and issue 'Feature-complete APNG optimization' is still open.
C or C++ applications that want an in-process library: there is only a Rust API and no C ABI, so use the CLI as a subprocess or write your own FFI shim.

Services processing untrusted or very large images under a hard deadline: --timeout is checked only between trials and does not stop a running compression, so set --max-raw-size; the libdeflater crate it depends on is looking for a new maintainer (issue #702, open, no decision).

integration.form: crate (library) and CLI binary; also distro packages, Windows release binaries and a Docker image
integration.dependencies: libdeflater (Rust binding to the C libdeflate library; feature system-libdeflate links the system copy), indexmap, rgb, rustc-hash, log; optional rayon (parallel, default), zopfli (default), clap, env_logger, parse-size and glob (binary feature, default), image (sanity-checks)
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.88.0 for 10.2.x (Cargo.toml rust-version, crates.io metadata; 1.85.1 for 10.0.0 to 10.1.1), edition 2024; the README still says 1.85.1
integration.platforms: any target Rust and libdeflate support; Docker images for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64; WASM used downstream (Squoosh, jSquash) but WASM tests in CI are an open issue
integration.thread_safety: optimize(), optimize_from_memory() and RawImage::create_optimized_png() are free functions taking an owned or borrowed Options with no shared mutable state beyond rayon's global pool; calling them from inside an existing rayon pool deadlocked before 9.0.0. Build without the parallel feature for single-threaded use, or cap threads with -t in the CLI.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: produces standard PNG files like OptiPNG and keeps similar -o levels and strip options, but the CLI is different (README: not a drop-in replacement) and its levels run different trial sets

gotchas: Version 10.0.0 renamed flags: -P/--pretend became -d/--dry-run, -Z became -z and --interlace takes on/off, so the README benchmark commands (oxipng -P) do not run on 10.x as written; the library API also changed (optimize() now returns original and optimized sizes, Deflaters became Deflater).

--alpha alters the color of fully transparent pixels (the README calls it technically lossy), and --scale16 forcibly scales 16-bit to 8-bit; both are off by default, but pipeline scripts copied from the web often include --alpha.
Default output removes interlacing (since 9.0.0); use -i keep to retain it, and interlacing is only applied when smaller unless --force is given.

The README's library snippet (version "10.0", features ["parallel", "zopfli", "filetime"], default-features = false) no longer builds: the filetime feature was dropped in 10.1.0 (crates.io feature lists for 10.1.0 to 10.2.1) without a changelog entry, and "10.0" resolves to 10.2.1; list only parallel and zopfli.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick oxipng when you already have PNG files and want them smaller with identical pixels; fpng, fpnge and mtpng are fast encoders from raw pixels whose files are larger (fpnge's catalogued ratio is about 15% worse than libpng's), and libspng, image-png and zune-png are decoders. ECT (catalogued under general-lossless) squeezes harder with its zopfli-derived deflate at a much higher run time.
verified_claims_summary: The v9.0.0 to v10.0.0 README timed a pre-release oxipng 9.0.0 (commit c16519b, rustc 1.74.0-nightly 2023-09-28, release profile lto = "thin", default features with rayon) against Debian's OptiPNG 0.7.7 with hyperfine on an Intel Core i7-12700 (20 threads): 59.6 ms versus 132.4 ms at the default level (2.22x) and 88.7 ms versus 444.9 ms at -o4 (5.01x), both in dry-run mode. The input is one 500x400 16-bit RGB PNG (116 KB) that both tools can losslessly reduce to 8-bit grayscale; output sizes were not reported, and at that commit -o4 meant four filter strategies (None, Bigrams, BigEnt, Brute) fully compressed with libdeflate level 12 in parallel, a different trial set from OptiPNG's -o 4, so the 5x is time-at-named-preset, not the same work done faster.
status_note: Actively developed (v10.2.1, last commit 2026-09-02, 4.3k stars), MIT and widely packaged; usable from C++ projects as a CLI build step rather than a linked library.
